open_errors.issue: In ch 3 the 'thirty-five days in a soft year' is the gap between the Meadow Cairn's meltwater and Shilak's. A soft year is said to widen that gap past three weeks. From ch 17 on, thirty-five days is the length of the bond itself, from the binding to the Meadow meltwater. Ch 30 (Meera) calls it a soft year, yet ch 31 puts Shilak's thaw only three weeks after day 35. Ch 17 also calls the three-week gap a hard-year figure.
open_errors.fix: Make ch 3's thirty-five days the bond's length in a soft year, with Shilak about three weeks behind the Meadow every year, and drop 'hard year' from ch 17.

patches.find: In a hard year the gap closed to three weeks. In a soft year it opened.
patches.replace: Shilak's water ran about three weeks behind the Meadow's, year on year. It was the Meadow's own date that moved.

patches.find: "Thirty-five days," she said. "In a soft year. That's what I lose."
patches.replace: "Thirty-five days from the binding," she said. "In a soft year. Then I lose the rope."

patches.find: The crown thinks I have the whole winter. I have the winter minus thirty-five days.
patches.replace: The crown thinks I have the whole winter. I have thirty-five days of it.

patches.find: After that, three weeks on in a hard year, the Shilak thaw council would sit
patches.replace: After that, about three weeks on, the Shilak thaw council would sit

open_errors.issue: Ch 16 says Ila swore the archive oath before the council clerk in the Garh Neshar hall, from a page that came with the summer post. She has been in Neshar since Book 1. Ch 23 says she swore it in a hall in Taravan.
open_errors.fix: Change ch 23 to the Garh Neshar hall.

patches.find: She had sworn in a hall in Taravan to keep what the crown's papers held
patches.replace: She had sworn in the Garh Neshar hall to keep what the crown's papers held

open_errors.issue: Ila hedges that the queen's letter 'did not say he had walked this way, only that he had been guided'. The letter (ch 16) says Udai guided Harish 'by the way that begins at these lakes'.
open_errors.fix: Make the hedge match the letter: it names the way but not what was done at its end.

patches.find: Hedged, even in her own head: the letter did not say he had walked this way, only that he had been guided.
patches.replace: Hedged, even in her own head: the letter said he had been guided this way, not what was done to him at its end.

open_errors.issue: In ch 7 Kunal says the map can spare Mini's star ('A star doesn't tell anyone where a hut is. I think we can spare it'). In ch 19 Ila says Kunal told her it wouldn't go on the map.
open_errors.fix: Have Ila report what Kunal actually said.

patches.find: Kunal said it wouldn't go on the map. It won't.
patches.replace: Kunal said the map could spare it. It won't go on.

open_errors.issue: Meera arrives the morning after Ila's private salt-house promise and speaks of 'your promise' and of 'two copies, identical, signed by both of you'. Ila made that promise alone with Kunal in the top room, and nobody has told Meera about it.
open_errors.fix: Make Meera's words general, so the specifics of the promise stay with Ila and Kunal.

patches.replace: Nineteen days any promise on that rope bites.

patches.find: Two copies, identical, signed by both of you before then.
patches.replace: Whatever you mean to lay before it, have it signed by then.

open_errors.issue: Chs 3, 4 and 12 say the east bearing never went into Ila's field book; she closed the book on a page without it. Chs 31 and 32 say she has it pencilled in the margin, but the book never shows her writing it.
open_errors.fix: Say in ch 31 that she pencilled it from memory at Ranu.

patches.find: In the margin of her field book she had one pencilled bearing: a faint broken line of cairn-light, seen going east in the dark.
patches.replace: In the margin of her field book she had one bearing, pencilled from memory at Ranu: a faint broken line of cairn-light, seen going east in the dark.

open_errors.issue: In ch 3 Ila recognises 'Three for the bend' and 'Four for the fold' as words she heard Kunal tap out for Chuni. In ch 2 she only appears at the door as he sings 'Nine and thirty', so she could not have heard the earlier lines.
open_errors.fix: Let ch 2 say she was in the passage for most of the song.

patches.find: She had walked in on the tune.
patches.replace: She had been in the passage for most of the tune.
